question: How many children did Michal (David's first wife) have?
summary: 2 Samuel 6:23 states Michal had no child to the day of her death. 2 Samuel 21:8 refers to "the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul" who were handed over to the Gibeonites to be impaled.

reconcile.connective: Defenders harmonize two ways: either Michal raised her sister Merab's sons (the adoption reading), or the Masoretic "Michal" at 21:8 is a copyist's slip for "Merab."

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, who catalogs this as an SAB contradiction, presses the plain Masoretic wording: 6:23 says Michal died childless, yet 21:8 calls five impaled men "the sons of Michal."

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "How many children did Michal (David's first wife) have?"

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament, on 2 Samuel 21:8 (1861-75)
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: Keil & Delitzsch treat this exact pair, reading the Masoretic 'Michal' at 21:8 as a copyist's mistake for 'Merab' (1 Sam 18:19), leaving 6:23 intact. Used as the row-surfaced harmonizer keyed to this passage, since Haley's specific coverage of this verse-pair could not be confirmed.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Merab, Michal's sister, was the wife of Adriel; but Michal adopted and brought up the boys under her care.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the contradiction by the adoption reading: the five sons were biologically Merab's, raised by the childless Michal.
excerpts.source_note_text: the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she brought up for Adriel--Merab, Michal's sister, was the wife of Adriel; but Michal adopted and brought up the boys under her care.
